BERT4Rec (1904.06690, §3.6) randomly replaces a proportion ρ of sequence items with a reserved [MASK] token and minimizes mean negative log-likelihood over masked positions, using full-catalog softmax and bidirectional context. Inference appends [MASK] and scores from that token’s final representation. The paper explicitly acknowledges the mismatch and adds training samples masking only the last item, describing this as fine-tuning-like; it does not specify an epoch-dependent interpolation between Cloze and terminal losses. Terminal masking itself is established prior art. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690)

Recency-based Sampling of Sequences (2207.02643, Algorithm 1) draws c=max(1,floor(nτ)) positions **with replacement**, with p(k)=α^(n−k)/Σj α^(n−j). Duplicate draws collapse; selected positions are removed entirely, preserving remaining order, and selected item IDs form a positive set. One sequence-level output predicts this set using LambdaRank with NDCG-swap-weighted gradients, or BCE in ablations; no negative sampling is used. Defaults: τ=0.2, α=0.8. α=1 gives uniform sampling; α→0 concentrates on the terminal position. Experiments compare fixed α values, not temporal annealing; BERT4Rec is a baseline rather than an RSS-trained architecture. [RSS](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643)

Neither cited paper evaluates L(t)=(1−λ(t))L_Cloze+λ(t)L_terminal with increasing λ. That schedule is a distinct experimental mechanism relative to their procedures, but novelty remains unestablished. Related later work, *From Past To Path* (2025), evaluates joint history reconstruction/next-item training, decreasing the masking ratio and finishing with next-item-only fine-tuning. It uses equal loss weights and semantic-ID generative models, so it supports reconstruction-to-prediction curricula without directly evaluating this BERT4Rec loss-weight schedule. [MHL, §§3.4–4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.23649v1)
